faq.q: Where were the mushrooms before it rained?
faq.a: The fungus that makes them was already living underground or in wood as a web of threads called mycelium. Only the mushrooms, its fruiting bodies, were missing.

faq.q: How can a mushroom grow overnight?
faq.a: The fungus prepares tiny buds with most of their cells already made. Rain lets those cells soak up water and stretch, so the mushroom inflates quickly instead of building new cells from scratch.
asks: How do mushrooms grow so fast?

faq.q: Why do mushrooms need damp weather?
faq.a: Mushrooms are mostly water and dry out quickly, and spores need moisture to sprout. Wet weather gives the best chance for spores to start new fungi.

faq.q: Do mushrooms grow in dry places?
faq.a: Fewer do. Some fungi in dry places fruit only after rare rains, and some, like puffballs, have tougher skins. Most mushrooms are found in damp woods, lawns and fields.
Many last only a few days. Once they have released their spores they soften, rot or get eaten by slugs, insects and other animals. The mycelium underground lives on.

facts: Mushrooms are made of about 90 percent water.
Many mushrooms expand from tiny pre-formed buds by taking in water, which is why they can appear overnight.
The mycelium that produces mushrooms can live for many years underground.
